newsitem.title: JAPAN: Canada PM seeks Japanese investment.
newsitem.headline: Canada PM seeks Japanese investment.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien, in Tokyo for a five-day visit, on Wednesday urged Japanese business leaders to invest in his country which he says is now enjoying a flourishing economy.
"Japanese investment is vital to Canada's economic prosperity, and an important creator of jobs for Canadians," Chretien told business executives during a luncheon meeting.

Chretien said his country's economy enjoyed almost no inflation and interest rates lower than they had been in 40 years. Canada's deficit, which was over six percent of gross domestic product at one time, is expected to be less than three percent in fiscal 1996/97, he said.
"Canada's economy has never before offered such an inviting investment climate," Chretien said.

Chretien said Japan was Canada's second most important source of portfolio investment, with the latest survey showing major Japanese financial institutions holding over $40 billion of Canadian government assets.

"For Canada and Japan, trade has been the pillar of our relationship," he said. Over 37 percent of Canada's gross domestic product depends on exports, and Japan is Canada's second-largest market after the United States.
The two countries agreed on Wednesday to promote cooperation between Japanese and Canadian companies in third-country markets in Asia and other parts of the world.
The agreement was reached during a meeting between Canadian International Trade Minister Arthur Eggleton and Japanese Trade Minister Shinji Sato.
Under the third-country partnership, the two countries will exchange information on infrastructure projects led by the private sector.
